procedure.description: bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty with excessive skin weighting down the lid

denial.carcText: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 15823 (bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty with excessive skin weighting down the lid) with date of service 2026-05-17. CARC 11: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure. Payer remark: The diagnosis reported does not support a functional indication for the procedure.

criteria.text: Visual field testing demonstrating at least 12 degrees of superior visual field loss, with improvement when the upper lids are taped.
Photographs documenting redundant upper lid skin resting on or over the lashes, or a margin reflex distance 1 of 2 millimeters or less.
A documented functional complaint such as difficulty reading or driving, loss of the superior field, or brow fatigue.

chart.text: Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 193, LDL 133, HDL 42, triglycerides 147. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

58 year old woman sent over by her eye doctor for heavy upper lids. Exam: marked dermatochalasis both upper lids, skin hooding over the lashes laterally, brow ptosis mild, no true ptosis of the lid itself, levator function good. Discussed upper lid blepharoplasty. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, anxiety, sees a counselor, seasonal allergies. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 14 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She says she is lifting her brows all day to see, gets a headache by evening, has given up night driving, tilts her head back to read the paper.

Humphrey superior field, untaped: 16 degrees of superior field remaining on the right and 14 on the left, which works out to about 37 percent loss of the superior field. Taped: improves to 35 right and 31 left. Reliable test, fixation losses low.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Blood pressure check. 123 over 78 today, 122 over 91 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
A1c came back 5.9. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Back to review the testing. Went over the operation, bruising, the scar in the crease, the small chance of dry eye. She wants to go ahead. Vitals today 128 over 87, pulse 88.
Frontal and lateral photos today, primary gaze, flash. Redundant upper lid skin draping onto the lashes on both sides. MRD1 about 2 millimeters right and 2 left.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the skin excision sitting up. No blood thinners. Stop the fish oil.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 11 denial can be answered from the record.
